extension_of.relationship: additive_extension; v0.3 remains immutable and is audited separately

purpose: Add known-answer checks for human-facing repairability, repair event phase accounting, post-repair verification, recurrence claim limits, and service-parts evidence. This extension does not measure actual user or technician performance; it checks an evaluator against synthetic scenarios.
claim_ceiling: This file is an unexecuted benchmark specification. Passing its software oracle does not mean user studies, physical repairs, service-parts continuity, appliance safety, or product durability have been demonstrated.
hard_invariants: A calculated repairability index cannot stand in for observed opening, access, or fault-identification tasks by the intended user population.
A failed hard access or non-destructive-service requirement cannot be compensated by a high aggregate score.
Diagnosis time, active labour, parts/tool waiting, verification time, rework, and total downtime are distinct quantities; missing phases must not be silently imputed as zero.
A repair counts as restored only within a declared scope and after post-repair function verification bound to the exact product/module revision.
A short follow-up with no observed recurrence does not prove lifetime reliability or a permanent repair.
A recurrence observed within the declared window must remain visible and must block a stronger durable-restoration claim.
A service-parts listing is not a current parts-availability or continuity commitment.
User and technician task outcomes, unsuccessful attempts, damage, and sample sizes must remain in the denominator and must not be silently omitted.
Human testing must not ask unqualified participants to undertake hazardous mains, induction-cooking, or refrigerant-system work.
A software audit of synthetic known answers is not a physical, human-factors, conformity, or service-network trial.

scenarios.title: Calculated repairability score has no observed user-task evidence
required_assertions: do not infer user repairability from the calculated index
observe opening and fault-identification tasks with an appropriate participant protocol
report the sample, task, unsuccessful attempts and limitations

scenarios.title: High score hides failed opening or access and permanent damage
required_assertions: failed non-destructive access remains a hard failure
aggregate score cannot offset permanent-structure damage
retain the failed attempt and damage in the report

scenarios.title: Observed user-task evidence passes only its defined accessibility scope
required_assertions: pass only the named user-task accessibility gate
retain sample size, task conditions, success rate and uncertainty
do not imply electrical safety or that participants may perform hazardous repairs

scenarios.title: Repair event records its full timeline and revision
required_assertions: keep diagnosis, active labour, wait, verification, rework and downtime separate
bind the record to the exact product/module revision
report failures and denominators instead of only successful repairs

scenarios.title: Repair report omits parts waiting while claiming low repair burden
required_assertions: missing parts/tool wait is unknown, not zero
do not publish a complete repair-burden claim from incomplete phase data
collect missing data or explicitly narrow the claim

scenarios.title: Component is repaired but post-repair verification is absent
required_assertions: do not count the repair as restored
require the scoped functional check and an evidence reference
separate repair attempt from verified restoration

scenarios.title: Post-repair function is verified on the exact revision
required_assertions: pass only the stated post-repair function check
retain exact revision, test conditions and evidence identity
do not infer long-term reliability from a single successful check

scenarios.title: Same failure recurs within a declared follow-up window
required_assertions: recurrence blocks the stated durable-restoration claim within this protocol
retain repair attempt, recurrence timing and probable cause as separate events
do not erase recurrence by counting the initial repair as an unconditional success

scenarios.title: Service part is listed but no current continuity evidence exists
required_assertions: a parts-list entry alone does not establish current availability or a future commitment
do not claim a parts-continuity horizon
obtain dated, exact-part-number evidence and disclose commitment limitations

scenarios.title: Current parts evidence supports only a scoped continuity statement
required_assertions: pass only the scoped, dated parts-evidence gate
distinguish a written policy from inventory on hand and a binding guarantee
expire or refresh time-sensitive evidence before relying on it

scenarios.title: Weighted repairability score attempts to compensate for a hard-gate failure
required_assertions: do not rank as feasible or repairable under the declared hard constraint
preserve reasons and failed-trial evidence
revise the architecture instead of increasing the aggregate score

proposed_software_benchmarks.definition: All repair records claiming complete burden data contain all declared timing phases and a revision binding; missing is not zero.
Every repair counted as restored has scoped post-repair verification evidence bound to the exact revision.
Every human-facing repairability claim is supported by observed user-task data or remains explicitly inconclusive.
Every parts-continuity claim resolves to dated evidence for the exact part and declared scope.
No aggregate score promotes a candidate that fails a declared non-compensable access or damage gate.

physical_and_human_studies_not_performed: Observed, non-hazardous opening and fault-identification tasks using an appropriate participant protocol
Qualified technician repairs with separately measured diagnosis, labour, waiting, verification, rework and downtime
Post-repair verification and pre-registered recurrence follow-up
